chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: Learning to read with Eugene Love's help
summary: Basic reading at Anderson High, then practice with pianist Eugene Love, enough showmanship to fool people.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But, I mean, you had become fairly proficient, obviously, on this B flat helicon, hadn't you?
I think I was just beginning to start fooling people, you know. I could read good, and --
Well, how did you learn? Who taught you to read, now.
Among us -- we had the basic learning in school, you know.
Oh, in high school you had that?
Yeah, but I didn't know how to apply it to the bass clef.
So we'd practice. We'd practice all evening, all night. The neighbors would complain about us boys. We were playing all out of tune, and everything. But we'd stay there and practice.
And we had a fellow named Clarence Love, played piano, next with Sammy Holmes' orchestra. And -- later played with Sammy Holmes' orchestra.

No, it was Eugene Love, not Clarence. And he would come over and he'd have patience, and we'd keep on until we played this first bar right. Let's go over it again until we got it, you know, one of those things. Just took an interest in the group. He'd play piano for us...
Oh, that was very helpful at that stage.
Yeah, he took an interest in our group. That kind of got us started. And then we had enough showmanship to fool the people, you know.
